title: Security posture discovery with Sentinel Finance
summary: Initial security posture discovery: customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for PII-sensitive financial analytics. Primary concerns: SOC 2 / ISO certification, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logging and retention, KMS integration and customer-managed keys, and data residency. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2/ISO artifacts, scheduling a private deployment architecture deep-dive, and running a demo of SSO and audit log exports.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Jordan Meyers: Send SOC 2 report + ISO27001 cert (2026-08-21)
Priya Shah: Share private deployment architecture diagram and VPC peering notes (2026-08-24)
Mina to provide list of compliance requirements and retention windows (2026-08-26)
Schedule a technical deep dive/demo (SE-led) for 60 mins week of 2026-08-31
action_items: Jordan Meyers: Upload security pack link to shared folder (due 2026-08-21)
Priya Shah: Prepare audit log retention export example (due 2026-08-24)
Tom Alvarez: Confirm list of regulatory controls for logging and encryption (due 2026-08-26)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-19 11:00am PT / 15:00Z; Duration ~52 mins; Attendees listed above

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time today. Quick intros?
[00:12] Tom (Sentinel): Hi, Tom Alvarez here, head of security at Sentinel Finance. We've got Mina who runs infra and Liam from product, and Sara from legal may chime in.
[00:20] Jordan: Great, thanks. Priya from our solutions engineering team is here too. We'll mostly run security questions and then map to hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda - certifications, identity, encryption/KMS, audit logs & retention, and deployment options. How does that sound?
[00:43] Mina (Sentinel): Sounds good. We're mainly worried about storing/processing PII and sensitive trading signals, so encryption and access controls are top for us.
[00:52] Jordan: Understood. To kick off - do you currently have any certification requirements we should be aware of? SOC 2 type II? ISO?
[01:02] Tom: Yes, SOC 2 type II is mandatory for us and our downstream customers. We're also in the process of pursuing ISO 27001. For any hosted vendor we expect SOC 2 and ideally evidence of ISO or a roadmap.
[01:15] Jordan: We can share our SOC 2 report and ISO artifacts - we'll put them in the security pack. For Redwood Hosted we have SOC 2 compliant operations; for Dedicated/Private customers we also provide enterprise attestation and options for on-site assessments.
[01:29] Liam (Sentinel): If we go Dedicated vs Private what's the real difference for us re compliance?
[01:36] Priya: Good question - Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and network controls but still runs in Redwood-managed infra; Private (VPC/private control plane or on-prem) gives you customer-managed networking and, depending on the model, the option to use your KMS/HSM. Private is the strongest for data residency and full control, but higher operational overhead.
[01:55] Mina: Can we use our own KMS in Dedicated?
[02:00] Priya: For Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys in many cases via a KMS integration, but the Private option gives the clearest path for CMKs/HSM and stricter SLAs around key separation. There are some architectural tradeoffs - we'll share the details.
[02:16] Sara (Sentinel Legal): For legal we'll need evidence of key separation and proof that Redwood cannot decrypt customer ciphertext.
[02:23] Jordan: Totally - we'll include KMS docs and a short note on how key management is implemented across deployment modes.
[02:30] Tom: Moving to identity - we use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. We need user provisioning + role mapping and session controls.
[02:41] Priya: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC, plus SCIM for automated provisioning. RBAC is granular - you can map SCIM groups to roles and enforce least privilege. There are session policies and admin roles documented.
[02:55] Tom: Any limitations on role hierarchy - we have cross-tenant support and some nested groups.
[03:02] Priya: Some enterprise directories do nested groups differently; SCIM mappings handle most cases but in complex scenarios we recommend a short POC to confirm mapping behavior. We often work with customers on mapping templates.
[03:16] Liam: Audit logs - what do they look like? We need immutable logs for requests, responses metadata (not raw PII), admin actions, API keys usage, and exports to our SIEM.
[03:27] Priya: Audit logs include request metadata, policy decisions, admin actions, deploy events, and model version changes. For hosted deployments we can stream logs to customer's S3/Cloud storage or forward to SIEM via syslog/agents. We redact content by default for certain endpoints; you can opt-in to include request/response bodies for dedicated/private if needed, with appropriate controls.
[03:49] Mina: Retention windows - we need 7 years for certain logs for regulatory reasons, is that supported?
[03:56] Jordan: By default Redwood has configurable retention; long-term retention is supported via exports to customer-managed storage (e.g., S3 with lifecycle). For hosted customers we can negotiate retention SLAs or set up exports. Longer retention for PII content has to follow data minimization - we usually recommend exporting only metadata and storing payloads only where necessary.
[04:17] Tom: Encryption at rest - is all data encrypted? Do you use CMEK?
[04:22] Priya: Yes, encryption at rest by default; for Hosted we use provider-managed keys, for Dedicated we can support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) in many cloud setups, and for Private you can always mount your key provider/HSM. We'll include the KMS integration matrix.
[04:38] Sara: For legal we need to see evidence of key lifecycle policies and key rotation frequency.
[04:43] Jordan: We'll include a key lifecycle summary and rotation policy.
[04:48] Tom: How do you handle data residency? Some of our customers require EU-only processing and storage.
[04:54] Priya: We have region-specific hosting and can pin model execution and storage to specific regions. Dedicated deployments can be provisioned in customer-preferred cloud regions; Private on-prem solves that fully. We'll add region availability notes.
[05:08] Liam: Latency vs cost is another tradeoff; if we go private on-prem we get the lowest network latency but have heavy ops cost.
[05:16] Priya: Exactly - we typically help customers do a cost/latency analysis. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization/profiles to reduce cost while meeting latencies.
[05:27] Tom: On logging, we need immutable audit trails - any WORM capability?
[05:32] Priya: For exports to customer storage you can enable object lock / WORM in S3; internally we maintain append-only logs for auditing. We can show architecture for the append-only pipeline.
[05:45] Mina: Does Redwood's control plane ever see raw model outputs? For compliance we prefer outputs not be persisted in provider logs.
[05:53] Jordan: By default, hosted pipelines may retain request/response metadata and short-lived cache for performance, but raw outputs are not persisted in logs unless you opt-in. For Dedicated/Private you get stronger guarantees and can disable persistence of outputs; we'll document defaults and opt-in behaviors.
[06:10] Sara: What about pen test and attestation? We require yearly pentest reports and vendor attestation.
[06:16] Jordan: Redwood runs regular security assessments; we can share pen test summaries and allow on-site assessments for Dedicated/Private customers under NDA.
[06:25] Tom: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for our vendor reviews.
[06:30] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide the subprocessors list and data flow diagrams.
[06:35] Liam: For a proof-of-concept can we get timeboxed access to a Dedicated pool? We want to run synthetic loads and validate KV cache behavior and latency.
[06:44] Priya: We can offer a POC - usually a short Dedicated eval or private test environment. We'll scope compute and runbench; Jordan will follow up on pricing and process.
[06:55] Tom: One more - SAML session lifetime and session revocation for compromised accounts.
[07:01] Priya: You can configure session timeouts and force session invalidation via admin APIs. SCIM deprovisioning removes access and we have immediate token revocation flows.
[07:12] Sara: Legal question about data deletion requests - how quickly can you delete customer data?
[07:17] Jordan: We support deletion requests; for hosted there are standard timelines and for Dedicated/Private we do faster on-prem removal. We'll add documented SLAs.
[07:25] Tom: Ok, this is helpful. What's the typical sprint to go from eval to Dedicated?
[07:30] Jordan: For Dedicated it's usually 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and networking approvals; Private on-prem can take longer. We'll run a migration checklist.
[07:40] Mina: Can we get a sample RBAC matrix?
[07:43] Priya: Yes, we'll share a template mapping SCIM groups to Redwood roles and examples.
[07:49] Liam: Any chance to demo streaming audit logs and a simulated export to our SIEM?
[07:54] Priya: Absolutely - that's part of the SE deep dive. We'll demonstrate log format, redaction, and export.
[08:02] Jordan: Recap and next steps - I'll send SOC2 and ISO docs, Priya will send architecture and demo invite, Mina/Tom to send regulatory specifics and retention windows. We'll tentatively schedule the SE deep dive week of 8/31.
[08:20] Tom: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:23] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up via email and CRM.
[08:27] End of call.
